shortDescription: Chip technology supplier Arm Holdings NASDAQ:ARM breached a licensing agreement with Qualcomm NASDAQ:QCOM and intentionally interfered with the chipmaker's business relationship with Meta Platforms NASDAQ:META, a Delaware jury found on Tuesday.

children: breached a licensing agreement with Qualcomm
and intentionally interfered with the chipmaker's business relationship with Meta Platforms
, a Delaware jury found on Tuesday.
The federal jury awarded Qualcomm nominal damages of just $2 from Arm, according to court records.
Shares of Arm were down 1% following the verdict, while shares of Qualcomm rose 1%.
The verdict followed a five-day trial last week, the second in two years between the companies that highlighted the deterioration of their business relationship after SoftBank Group
acquired control of Arm in 2016 and Arm shifted from licensing the technology needed to make chips to selling chips of its own.
